theory.intro: Large areas of land are measured in hectares (ha) and square kilometres (km$^2$) rather than square metres.
facts: $1\text{ ha} = 10\,000\text{ m}^2$ (a square $100$ m by $100$ m).
Use **ha** for paddocks, parks and sports grounds; use **km$^2$** for suburbs, forests and countries.
steps: Decide whether the area is land-sized (ha) or region-sized (km$^2$).
To convert m$^2$ to ha, divide by $10\,000$.
To convert ha to km$^2$, divide by $100$ (or m$^2$ to km$^2$ divide by $1\,000\,000$).

foundation.question_text: Choose the more suitable unit for the area of a community garden: hectares or square kilometres.
foundation.solution_text:
A community garden is land-sized rather than region-sized.
Hectares are more suitable.

foundation.question_text: Choose the more suitable unit for the area of a large national park: hectares or square kilometres.
foundation.solution_text:
A large national park covers a region-sized area.
Square kilometres are more suitable.

development.question_text: A wetland covers $45\,000\text{ m}^{2}$. Record its area in hectares.
Which is larger: $80$ ha or $0.9\text{ km}^{2}$?
development.solution_text:
$0.9\text{ km}^{2}$
$=90\text{ ha}$
$90\text{ ha}>80\text{ ha}$
$0.9\text{ km}^{2}$ is larger.

development.question_text: A land record states an area of $320\,000\text{ m}^{2}$. Write this area in both hectares and square kilometres.

mastery.question_text: Three reserves cover $85$ ha, $0.7\text{ km}^{2}$ and $900\,000\text{ m}^{2}$. Order them from smallest to largest.
mastery.solution_text:
$0.7\text{ km}^{2}=70\text{ ha}$
$900\,000\text{ m}^{2}=90\text{ ha}$
$70\text{ ha}<85\text{ ha}<90\text{ ha}$
From smallest to largest: $0.7\text{ km}^{2}$, $85$ ha, $900\,000\text{ m}^{2}$.

mastery.question_text: A conservation area contains two parcels of $1.25\text{ km}^{2}$ and $65$ ha. Find the total area in hectares.
A report describes a small school oval as covering $12\text{ km}^{2}$. Explain why the unit is unreasonable and give a more suitable large-area unit.
mastery.solution_text:
$12\text{ km}^{2}=1\,200\text{ ha}$, which is region-sized rather than school-oval-sized.
Hectares would be the more suitable large-area unit.
